subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Butter Tea of Tibet
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Butter Tea of Tibet.

hook.text: Tibetans drink tea mixed with yak butter and salt—a savory, high-calorie drink essential for high-altitude survival.

buildup.text: Tea bricks are boiled for hours, then churned in a wooden cylinder with butter and salt until creamy.

discovery.text: At 4,000+ meters, the body burns enormous calories. Butter tea provides fat, salt, and warmth in a single cup.

twist.text: Tibetans drink 40–60 cups per day during cold months. The cup is constantly refilled, and refusing is considered rude.

climax.text: Butter tea is more like a savory soup than a drink. It sustained Tibetan civilization at Earth's highest altitudes for centuries.

punchline.text: Yak butter, salt, tea, altitude. Survival tastes different at 4,000 meters.

quiz.question: Why do Tibetans add yak butter and salt to tea?
options: The high calories and salt are essential for surviving at extreme altitude

details.summary: Tibetan butter tea, or po cha, is made by churning brewed black tea with yak butter and salt. The rich, savory drink provides essential calories and fat in Tibet's extreme high-altitude climate. It is consumed throughout the day, sometimes dozens of cups, and is central to Tibetan hospitality.
details.whyItMatters: Butter tea shows how tea adapts to extreme environments. In Tibet, tea is not a delicate beverage but a survival food essential for life above 4,000 meters.
takeaways: Butter tea is brewed tea churned with yak butter and salt
It provides essential calories in Tibet's extreme climate
Tibetans may drink dozens of cups throughout the day

faq.question: What does butter tea taste like?
faq.answer: It tastes more like a savory, salty broth than sweet tea. The yak butter gives it a rich, fatty mouthfeel. The taste can be surprising to outsiders expecting sweet tea, but in the thin, cold air of the Tibetan plateau it is deeply satisfying and warming.

faq.question: Why do Tibetans add butter and salt instead of sugar?
faq.answer: At altitudes above 4,000 meters, the body burns calories rapidly and dehydrates quickly. Butter provides fat and calories. Salt aids hydration. Together they make tea a genuine survival food rather than just a beverage. The recipe is a practical adaptation to extreme living conditions.
